page.text:
A *group* is a monoid in which every element possesses a two-sided
inverse: for each $x \in G$, there exists an element $y \in G$ satisfying
$x * y = e$ and $y * x = e$.

Groups constitute the foundational paradigm of modern algebra. While
monoids can represent irreversible processes (such as non-injective
functions or lossy data compression), groups formalize the geometry of
*reversible transformations* and *symmetries*. Historically conceived by
Évariste Galois in 1832 to characterize the solvability of polynomial
equations by radicals, groups now permeate every branch of modern
mathematics and theoretical physics, from crystallography and quantum
mechanics to gauge theory and algebraic topology.
